Read an h5ad file as a SingleCellExperiment

Source: R/h5ad.R
readH5adAsSCE.Rd

Reads the AnnData on-disk format (anndata 0.8 or later) directly from HDF5 with rhdf5, without Python or zellkonverter, and returns a SingleCellExperiment. From there the object can go to convertSCEToCerebro, or to any other tool that reads SCE.

Usage

readH5adAsSCE(
  file,
  use_raw = FALSE,
  modality = NULL,
  gene_names = NULL,
  airr = "auto",
  airr_sample = NULL,
  spatial_images = "auto",
  extra_modalities = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  .root = NULL
)

Arguments

file

Path to a .h5ad file, or a .h5mu (MuData) file together with modality. Files written by anndata before 0.7 (compound-dataset layout, raw.X) are read too.

use_raw

Use raw/X (and raw/var) as the expression matrix, as scanpy workflows often keep the full, unfiltered gene set there. layers are then not read, because their genes differ.

extra_modalities

For a MuData file: other modalities to read next to the expression one (for example "prot" for antibody counts), or "all" for every modality except the expression and receptor ones. Each becomes an alternative experiment of the result, with its own features and the cells of the expression modality (cells it lacks get zeros).

modality

For a MuData file (.h5mu), the modality to read, e.g. "gex". Optional when the file has one modality or one obviously expression-like name (rna, gex).

gene_names

Name of a var column to use as the gene names, e.g. "feature_name" (CELLxGENE) or "gene_symbols". By default the var index is used, except when it is made of Ensembl IDs and such a column exists. The original index stays in rowData as var_index.

airr

Immune receptor data to import: "auto" (default) uses the MuData modality named airr, or obsm["airr"] of a plain h5ad, if the file has one and imports nothing otherwise. Give a name to use another modality (or obsm entry); FALSE or NULL skips receptor data. The AIRR modality is never taken for the expression modality.

airr_sample

Column of obs that names the sample of each cell, which keys the immune repertoire. By default orig.ident, sample, Sample or sample_id is used if present, else all cells are one sample ("Sample_1").

spatial_images

Which Visium tissue images to embed: "auto" (default; hires when present, otherwise lowres), a character vector of image labels ("hires", "lowres", "fullres"), or FALSE for none. Needs the png package.

verbose

Print what was skipped.

.root

Internal: HDF5 group that holds the data set (used for the modalities inside a MuData file). Leave NULL.

Value

A SingleCellExperiment with genes in rows and cells in columns. Duplicate gene names are made unique with a message; duplicate cell names are an error.

Details

The mapping is:

  • X becomes the assay "X"; each entry of layers becomes an assay of the same name (so layers["counts"] is the assay "counts").

  • obs / var become colData / rowData. Categorical, string, boolean and nullable integer/boolean/string columns are all decoded; missing values stay NA.

  • obsm entries with at least two numeric columns become reducedDims; a leading X_ is dropped and pca, umap and tsne are upper-cased (X_umap is "UMAP").

  • scanpy's uns["rank_genes_groups"] results become metadata(sce)$marker_genes, one table per groupby variable; marker tables written by exportToH5ad under uns["cerebro"]["marker_genes"] are read back as they were.

  • immune receptor chains written by scirpy (an awkward array in obsm["airr"], or the airr modality of a MuData file) become metadata(sce)$immune_repertoire: a list named by sample, one row per cell with barcode, CTgene, CTnt, CTaa and CTstrict, assembled into clones by scRepertoire as on the Seurat route. Only productive chains of TCR/BCR loci with a CDR3 (junction_aa) count; a cell that shows both TCR and BCR chains keeps the type with more chains (then more UMIs). Cells are matched to the expression data by name.

  • trajectories become metadata(sce)$trajectories, the structure of object@misc$trajectories. For every pseudotime column in obs (dpt_pseudotime, velocity_pseudotime, latent_time, any *_pseudotime) one trajectory is made per source: scanpy's PAGA (uns["paga"]) as method "paga", with the groups as nodes at the centroid of their cells in the UMAP (t-SNE) and the connectivities of at least 0.01 as edges; scVelo's obsm["velocity_<basis>"] as method "scvelo", the velocity averaged on a grid (25 x 25 at most) and drawn as arrows; and, when the file has neither, just the pseudotime as method "pseudotime". The velocity_* entries of obsm are not embeddings and are not added to reducedDims. Gene-level velocity (layers velocity) and the directed PAGA transitions are not used.

  • scanpy's category colours (uns["<column>_colors"]) become metadata(sce)$group_colors, a named vector (level to colour) per categorical column, and are applied as the default colours of those groups in the Viewer. A column is used only when it has one valid colour for each of its levels.

  • Visium tissue images in uns["spatial"][<library_id>]["images"] become metadata(sce)$spatial_images, one entry per library, each with its image as an embedded PNG and its extent in spot-coordinate space: spot coordinates (obsm["spatial"]) are full-resolution pixels and an image is the full-resolution picture scaled by its tissue_*_scalef, so it covers [0, width/scale] by [0, height/scale]. The image keeps its own orientation (row 0 on top); flip it for display in the Spatial tab, as for Seurat objects.

Sparse X (CSR or CSC) and dense X are supported. A CSR matrix is used as it is, because the CSR of cells x genes is the CSC of genes x cells. Other uns, obsp, varm and varp content is not read.

See also

convertH5adToCerebro, convertSCEToCerebro

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sce <- readH5adAsSCE("pbmc.h5ad")
convertSCEToCerebro(sce, "output", groups = "cell_type")
} # }
